versions.summary: The profile centers on mathematically grounded machine learning for variable-size structured data, especially invariant and equivariant architectures, size transferability, graph limits, and universality, with a second core emphasis on learned proximal operators for diffusion models and inverse problems.

topics.name: Any-dimensional learning and size generalization
evidence: Four core seeds study models that operate across changing input sizes, including universality, transferability, equivariant extensions, and graphon limits.
The selected domains include graphs, sets, point clouds, and particle systems.

topics.name: Invariant and equivariant neural networks
evidence: Core papers focus on symmetry-aware architectures, representation stability, invariant graph networks, and universality under invariance.
The preference spans both architectural design and rigorous expressivity analysis.

topics.name: Theory of machine learning
evidence: All six core seeds emphasize formal guarantees, structural characterizations, convergence, approximation, or transfer principles.
The evidence favors papers combining mathematical theory with architecture design or experiments.

topics.name: Graph neural networks and graph limits
evidence: Core seeds cover graph parameters across sizes, graphons, higher-order GNNs, invariant graph networks, and size transferability.
Graph-limit geometry and expressivity beyond message passing are recurring interests.

topics.name: Learned proximal operators and regularization
evidence: Two core seeds develop learned proximal maps with theoretical guarantees for data-driven priors, inverse problems, and generative sampling.
The user selected both the foundational proximal-matching work and its diffusion-model extension.

topics.name: Diffusion and generative modeling
evidence: A core seed replaces score-based forward discretization with learned proximal maps in reverse-time SDE sampling.
This is a strong but currently narrower signal than the any-dimensional learning cluster.

topics.name: Inverse problems
evidence: A core seed studies learned proximal networks as exact operators for data-driven nonconvex regularizers with convergence guarantees.
The interest is tied specifically to interpretable learned priors and principled optimization.

methods: Invariant and equivariant neural architecture design
Graphon neural networks and higher-order GNNs
mathematics: Proximal operator theory and nonconvex regularization

versions.summary: The profile is centered on rigorous machine learning theory for models that operate across variable input sizes, with core interests in any-dimensional universality and size transferability. Secondary interests include equivariant and graphon neural networks, learned proximal operators, diffusion models, and inverse problems.

topics.name: Any-dimensional learning and size generalization
evidence: Two core seeds directly study universality and transferability for models defined across varying input dimensions.
Two interested seeds extend the theme through equivariant architectures and graphon-based size transferability.

topics.name: Invariant and equivariant neural networks
evidence: A core seed studies invariant universality using symmetries and limit spaces.
Interested seeds cover representation-stable equivariant networks and invariant graphon networks.

topics.name: Theory of machine learning
evidence: The core selections emphasize continuity, topology, universality, and architecture-level transfer guarantees.
All interested selections also favor convergence, expressivity, or approximation results over purely empirical modeling.

topics.name: Graph neural networks and graph limits
evidence: Two interested seeds address graph parameters across sizes, graphons, higher-order GNNs, and invariant graph networks.
The core transferability papers also use graphs as an important application domain, but graph-specific work was not labeled core.

topics.name: Learned proximal operators and regularization
evidence: Two interested seeds use learned proximal maps for principled priors, inverse problems, and generative sampling.
The repeated signal is meaningful but remains secondary because both submissions were labeled interested.

topics.name: Diffusion and generative modeling
evidence: One interested seed develops proximal diffusion models using backward discretization of reverse-time SDEs.
This is a narrow exploratory signal rather than a core preference.

topics.name: Inverse problems
evidence: One interested seed studies learned proximal networks for inverse problems with convergence guarantees.
The evidence supports exploratory interest in interpretable learned priors, not a strong standalone preference.
